## Daniel 9: Research notes

### v. 1
- **Who "Darius" is (views differ):** The Bible Hub study notes date the chapter to about 538 BC and say Darius the Mede is probably Gubaru (Gaubaruva). https://biblehub.com/daniel/9.htm
- Sam Storms reads it differently: Daniel prays "in the first year of Darius, son of Xerxes" (9:1-2), i.e., in the first year of Cyrus's reign (539-38 b.c.). https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/daniels-70-weeks
- Guzik (Enduring Word) points out that God's plan used people: Jeremiah gave a prophecy, Daniel prayed, and Cyrus issued a proclamation. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-9/

### v. 2
- **Scripture shapes prayer:** Guzik says Daniel understood the prophecy from inspired written books. Prophecy is meant to be understood, at least in its main points, if not every detail. Daniel took the 70 years as real, literal years, not symbols. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-9/
- **Praying early:** Guzik lists three deportations (605, 597 and 587 BC). He thinks Daniel was asking God to count from the earliest one, and notes Daniel started praying three or four years before the 70 years ran out. God's promises invite prayer rather than replace it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-9/
- Storms makes the same point: if the count began in 605 BC, 66 years had elapsed. Daniel does not wait fatalistically for the next four years to tick away. He also notes that Chapter 9 is the only chapter in Daniel in which the peculiarly covenantal name of God, *Yahweh*, occurs. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/daniels-70-weeks
- Jamieson, Fausset & Brown date the start of Jeremiah's 70 years to 606 B.C., eighteen years before the destruction of Jerusalem, for then Judah ceased to exist as an independent theocracy. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Dan/Dan_009.cfm
- Coffman notes that the captivity actually turned out to be only about 68 or 69 years. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/9-26.html

### v. 3
- Guzik: "I set my face" shows determination, like someone who will not be turned away, because he was sure his request was God's will. Fasting, sackcloth and ashes are signs of humility and mourning. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-9/

### v. 4
- Guzik: Daniel begins by recognising God's greatness and goodness. We sometimes come to God as if he were stingy and had to be talked into giving, but Daniel knew the problem was never on God's side. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-9/
- The BSB footnote says the Hebrew *chesed* ("loving devotion") covers love, kindness, faithfulness, mercy and loyalty to a covenant. https://biblehub.com/daniel/9.htm
- JFB on "great and dreadful God": as we know to our cost by the calamities we suffer. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Dan/Dan_009.cfm

### vv. 5–6
- Guzik: Daniel's confession used 'we' instead of 'they,' identifying with Israel's sin rather than standing apart. Measured against God, even the most righteous person falls short. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-9/
- The Bible Hub notes describe a pattern: humility, honouring God's character, confessing as a group, agreeing that God's judgment is just, then boldly asking. They compare Nehemiah 1 and Ezra 9. https://biblehub.com/daniel/9.htm

### vv. 7–8
- Guzik: the shame belonged to Israel, not God. Daniel confessed instead of complaining. Guzik adds J. Edwin Orr's advice that real confession is sincere, specific and thorough. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-9/

### vv. 9–10
- Guzik: Daniel offers no excuse at all. We tend to slip excuses even into our confessions. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-9/

### vv. 11–12
- Guzik: even in judgment God kept his word. He had promised curses on a disobedient Israel (Leviticus 26, Deuteronomy 28), and they came. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-9/

### v. 13
- Guzik: Daniel also confesses the sin of prayerlessness. Hard times should drive us straight to prayer, and if they don't, that is a warning about a cold heart. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-9/

### v. 14
- Bible Hub's lesson notes: God's justice is perfect and his ways are right even when we don't fully understand them. https://biblehub.com/daniel/9.htm

### v. 15
- Guzik: He remembers the Old Testament standard of God's power, the deliverance from Egypt. The New Testament standard of God's power is the resurrection of Jesus. https://www.blueletterbible.org/comm/guzik_david/study-guide/daniel/daniel-9.cfm

### v. 16
- Guzik on "according to all Your righteousness": Daniel isn't asking God to act against his righteousness. He is praying for it to be displayed. https://www.blueletterbible.org/comm/guzik_david/study-guide/daniel/daniel-9.cfm

### v. 17
- Guzik: "Cause your face to shine" is the heart of Daniel's plea. https://www.blueletterbible.org/comm/guzik_david/study-guide/daniel/daniel-9.cfm

### v. 18
- Bible.org (Deffinbaugh's series) dwells on this line about asking on the basis of God's mercies, not our own righteousness. It imagines how much the prayer must have delighted God. https://bible.org/seriespage/9-prophecy-seventy-weeks
- *Catholic angle:* A footnote in New Advent's Bible says Daniel's prayer has several points in common with that of the Jewish people in Bar. 1.15, 2.13. (Baruch is in the Catholic canon.) https://www.newadvent.org/bible/dan009.htm

### v. 19
- Guzik: Daniel asks God to act without delay, for God's own sake. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-9/

### vv. 20–21
- The Bible Hub notes say Gabriel first appeared in 8:16. "Swift flight" shows God's eagerness to answer. Daniel marks the time by the evening sacrifice even though the temple lies in ruins, so he still keeps time by God's schedule. https://biblehub.com/daniel/9.htm
- The Catholic Encyclopedia says Gabriel brought the prophecy of the seventy weeks of years which should elapse before the coming of Christ. It links him to his later announcements to Zechariah and Mary. https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/06330a.htm

### vv. 22–23
- Guzik: In his prayer, Daniel didn't ask for understanding. His prayer demonstrated that his heart was close to God's heart, so as a friend, God revealed many things to Daniel. Study alone hadn't unlocked Jeremiah for him; prayer did. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-9/
- Coffman: "understand the vision" probably points back to an earlier vision. He quotes a source saying this revelation came while Daniel was fully awake, not in a vision. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/daniel-9.html

### v. 24 (the six goals)
- **"Weeks" means sevens of years:** GotQuestions says almost all commentators agree that the seventy "sevens" should be understood as seventy "weeks" of years, in other words, a period of 490 years. https://www.gotquestions.org/seventy-weeks.html. Ellicott says the "year-week" idea rests on Numbers 14:34, Leviticus 26:34 and Ezekiel 4:6. https://biblehub.com/daniel/9-24.htm
- **Dispensational view (GotQuestions):** the prophecy summarizes what happens before Jesus sets up His millennial kingdom. But the atonement goal was met at the cross. https://www.gotquestions.org/seventy-weeks.html. The Bible Hub notes take a middle line: Christ's first coming won the atonement and his second coming finishes the rest. https://biblehub.com/daniel/9-24.htm
- **All six fulfilled at Christ's first coming (Coffman):** He applies all six to the first coming. He reads "anoint the Most Holy" as Christ himself and notes the old Syriac version renders it "to the Messiah, the Most Holy." He also reports that Keil (a Lutheran scholar) took the phrase as a thing, not a person. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/9-26.html
- **Symbolic or "jubilee" readings:** Storms says 10 jubilees = 490 years! The meaning of the period, therefore, is THEOLOGICAL, not calendrical. He quotes a source on "seal up vision and prophecy": the age of preparatory visions is closed off because the Messianic age has come. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/daniel-9:1-27. The Bridgeway commentary also takes the seventy weeks as symbolic of the new era about to begin. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/9-9.html
- **Ancient versions:** The Pulpit Commentary allows that some puzzles here may come from a damaged text. It lists how Theodotion, Tertullian's Old Latin and Jerome rendered the verse. https://biblehub.com/daniel/9-24.htm

### v. 25 (start date and "Messiah the Prince")
- **Dispensational count:** GotQuestions starts with Artaxerxes' decree to Nehemiah in about 444 BC. It uses 360-day years and arrives at AD 33, the time of Jesus' triumphal entry. https://www.gotquestions.org/seventy-weeks.html. Gaebelein starts in Nisan 445 BC. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/gab/daniel-9.html
- **Older Protestant count:** JFB starts with the return of Ezra to Jerusalem, 457 B.C. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/Dan/Dan_009.cfm
- **Against the 444 BC start:** Storms quotes the argument that the 70 weeks begin around 538 BC, and that a start in 444 BC would not really answer Daniel's prayer. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/daniel-9:1-27
- **Caution on exact dates:** Coffman says the start date is uncertain and that the "weeks of years" idea is assumed rather than proven. He cites Thomson, who counts from 445 BC and lands near AD 25 (Jesus' baptism) and AD 32. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/9-26.html
- **Modern scholarship:** Utley (on bible.org, citing the NET Bible) notes that many scholars and commentators have understood "anointed one" to refer to Cyrus II, and that they connect vv. 26–27 to Antiochus IV. https://bible.org/seriespage/daniel-9. The Expositor's Bible (1887) says most modern scholars, even Keil, follow the Hebrew punctuation that separates the seven weeks from the sixty-two. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/nas/daniel/9-27.html

### v. 26 ("cut off," "the prince who is to come")
- **Christ's death and Rome:** Adam Clarke (Methodist) says "the prince" is Titus and his "people" are the Romans who destroyed the temple. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/9-26.html
- **Dispensational "gap":** Precept Austin says the crucifixion comes just after the 69th week but not inside the 70th, because a gap lies between them. That gap is the church age. https://www.preceptaustin.org/daniel_927
- **Against a gap:** Storms argues that events "after" the 69th week happen "in" the 70th. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/daniels-70-weeks
- **Critical view:** Peake's Commentary says most modern scholars think it refers to Onias III, who, in 175 B.C., was deposed from the high priesthood by Antiochus Epiphanes. It calls "shall have nothing" an uncertain text. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/pfc/daniel-9.html
- **Catholic translation:** The Knox rendering on New Advent reads that the people will disown him and have none of him. https://www.newadvent.org/bible/dan009.htm

### v. 27 (who "confirms the covenant"?)
This is where the traditions really part ways.
- **Reformed: it is Christ.** Calvin says the angel continues his discourse concerning Christ. He takes "many" to mean the faithful Gentiles united with the Jews. https://www.ccel.org/c/calvin/comment3/comm_vol25/htm/iv.xx.htm. The Geneva Bible notes say Christ affirmed his promise, first to the Jews, and after to the Gentiles and ended the sacrifices by his death and resurrection. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/daniel/9-27.htm
- **Methodist: it is Christ.** Wesley's Notes say Christ confirmed the new covenant through testimony, preaching, signs, his holy life, his resurrection and his death. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/9-27.html. Benson stresses that the covenant is made with "many," not all. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/daniel/9-27.htm
- **Lutheran:** On this page Keil & Delitzsch (labelled Lutheran) only lay out the options, such as reading "one week" as the subject following Theodotion. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/9-27.html. Coffman cites Keil saying most Church Fathers saw Christ, his death and AD 70 here. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/9-26.html
- **Dispensational: it is the Antichrist.** Precept Austin argues that Christ's ministry lasted three and a half years, not seven, and that sacrifices went on for about 40 years after the cross, so Clearly, the "he" is not Christ. https://www.preceptaustin.org/daniel_927. GotQuestions says the Antichrist rules only until his decreed end. https://www.gotquestions.org/seventy-weeks.html. Smith's Bible Commentary expects a rebuilt temple and a covenant made by a European leader. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/9-9.html
- **Charismatic voices disagree with each other.** Guzik (Enduring Word) follows a timeline that leads to the triumphal entry. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-9/. Storms (quoting Kline) says the first half of Daniel's 70th week runs from the baptism of Jesus to 70 a.d. The destruction of Jerusalem and its temple in 70 a.d. is the middle of the week, and the present church age is its latter half. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/daniels-70-weeks
- **Ellicott (neutral):** the subject is ambiguous. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/9-27.html
- **The "abomination":** Coffman links it to Jesus' words in Matthew 24:15. He takes it as the Zealots defiling the temple (from Josephus) before Rome destroyed it, and thinks it may happen again in the end times. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/9-26.html
- **Modern scholarship (Antiochus):** Peake reads the covenant as one Antiochus made with apostate Jews. It also objects that Jesus' ministry lasted only three years. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/pfc/daniel-9.html
- **The Gospel Coalition's overview** sets out the Onias III/Antiochus view, the dispensational view and others, and notes that some of these do not culminate in Christ. They culminate either in Antiochus or they culminate in the Antichrist. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/sermon/daniel-7-12-part-2/

### Catholic and Orthodox (whole prophecy)
- The Catholic Encyclopedia names three main readings. The first, "traditional" one maintains that the prophecy of the seventy weeks refers directly to the appearance of Christ in the flesh, His death, His establishment of the New Covenant, and the destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans. The second, held mostly by non-Catholic scholars, applies the passage to Antiochus Epiphanes. https://www.catholic.com/encyclopedia/book-of-daniel. The third, held by some Church Fathers, reads it as the growth of God's kingdom up to Christ's second coming. https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/04621b.htm
- Origen wrote that according to Daniel, seventy weeks were fulfilled until (the coming of) Christ the Ruler. https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/04124.htm
- I found no Orthodox (oca.org) material on this chapter.

### Popular modern teaching
I found nothing on these sites linking Daniel 9 to prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace teaching. The popular debate that does show up is the dispensational seven-year tribulation and rebuilt temple (Precept Austin, GotQuestions, Smith).
